description: Public claims registry for f7-platform/public-docs. Maps each public-facing claim to its source evidence, audit references, and current release status. Used by scripts/check-public-claims.sh and reviewed each release cycle. `audit_run` below is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the public audit-run baseline: no other file in this repo may hardcode it, every other public 'Run N' mention is enforced against it by scripts/check-public-claims.sh, and it is bumped with `npm run bump:audit-run -- <N>`. Version 2 of this registry (2026-09-13) describes Atlas only: the claims about the earlier device-agent and controller product (CLM-001 to CLM-011) were retired with that product, and the numbering continues from CLM-012.

claims.summary: Trust Center dependency audit runs before GitHub Pages publication
evidence: public-docs: .github/workflows/deploy.yml — runs npm audit --audit-level=moderate before claim checks and build
public-docs: scripts/check-public-claims.sh — rejects overbroad every-commit/every-code-change dependency-audit claims
claims.notes: This claim is scoped to the public-docs Trust Center deploy workflow; product dependency evidence is release-scoped in the owning private repository.

claims.summary: Atlas Rewind captures picture-only screen frames with consent; hosted submission to F7 is planned and not built
evidence: public-docs: content/legal/privacy-policy.md — the Atlas Rewind subsection: picture-only capture, no audio, the per-capture model read, and submission labelled planned and not built
public-docs: content/privacy/data-collection.md — the Atlas Rewind section, which restates the legal subsection in the same terms
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/rewind-config.ts — capture is picture-only at a fixed frame rate
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/build-profile.ts — the recorder is reachable only on a development server or an internal reference build, so no customer deployment shows it

fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/components/RewindFirstRun.tsx — the in-product explainer states picture-only capture, no audio, and that asking for a read sends that capture's stills and words to the configured model provider
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — the in-app policy's Rewind section, which these pages must agree with
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/terms-of-use.md — the consent clause: recorded against the deployment, revocable, never implied by a plan or licence tier
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/air_gap.rs — a cell that declared itself air-gapped withholds the Rewind submit path, and a session it should not have been able to open is raised as a finding

NOTE: the hosted submission path is designed and NOT built — no submit path exists in any shipped build and no customer deployment has been granted the recorder, so every sentence about submitting is labelled planned both on the page and here
claims.notes: Registered ahead of the feature by deliberate rule: the privacy policy and every public surface describing Rewind must be updated before any customer sees the recorder, so this claim exists while the control is still partly planned. TRUE TODAY: capture is picture-only with no audio; a capture stays on the customer's own Atlas instance; the one egress that exists is the reviewer asking a model to read the frames they selected, consented per capture; and the recorder is absent from every customer deployment. PLANNED, and must not be answered as a current control on a vendor questionnaire: submitting a capture to F7, and everything a submission carries. Retention of a submitted capture is deliberately unsettled (left to legal review on 2026-09-09), so the pages state that it is not yet set. Who at F7 may open a submitted capture was ruled on 2026-09-09: state today's answer as today's. soc2_criteria is deliberately empty until submission is built and counsel has reviewed the clause.

claims.summary: Atlas is a single-tenant instance — one deployment, one database, one signed ledger per customer — offered as a self-contained download or as an instance F7 operates
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 1: one deployment, one database, one signed ledger per customer; the two deployment models and who has access under each
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/bundled_pg.rs — the private PostgreSQL the download supervises, so nothing else has to be installed
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/export/mod.rs — the export refuses to run when the single-tenant premise cannot be verified (CannotVerifySingleTenantPremise)

fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/license/mod.rs — licences verify offline against the F7 keyset compiled into packaged builds, and the packaged 14-day offline trial, so the download runs with no route to F7
public-atlas-binaries: README.md — one download is the whole product; the web app is compiled into the binary and it starts its own private PostgreSQL
NOTE: hosted instances run on Railway infrastructure in the United States; the in-app policy states that F7 does not currently operate instances outside the United States
claims.notes: The isolation claim is the absence of a shared store, not a row filter. Do not describe hosted instances as multi-tenant or as isolated by row-level security.

claims.summary: The complete list of what leaves an Atlas instance: the configured AI provider (through F7's gateway on credit plans), optional voice, sources fetched on request with an operator-disableable rendering fallback, connected repositories, email, licensing, and the download's signed update check
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 4, the list of outside services and the purposes for each

fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-llm/src/config.rs — the provider kinds (Anthropic and Gemini with dedicated drivers; OpenAI-compatible endpoints including OpenRouter, Ollama, Groq and custom), per-feature routing, and credentials kept out of the configuration file
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/llm/metered_provider.rs — on credit plans the turn is relayed through F7's gateway to the provider and metered there
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/gateway_client/mod.rs — the credit-gateway session exists only in credit mode; a bring-your-own-key deployment mints no keypair and opens no session
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/config.rs — the voice provider (ElevenLabs), the GitHub connection credentials, and the update configuration
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/vault_ingest/fetch.rs — the default third-party rendering fallback (r.jina.ai) for pages that cannot be read directly
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/email/smtp.rs — the SMTP backend for verification, password-reset and invitation mail
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/update.rs — the signed update-manifest check, present only on the packaged download
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/diagnostics.ts — an error report is assembled in the browser and nothing transmits on its own
claims.notes: This list is published as complete. Adding an outbound integration to the product requires adding it here and to every page that states the list.

claims.summary: Account security: Argon2id password hashing, time-based one-time codes with an encrypted secret, passkeys, hashed single-use recovery codes, durable lockout, revocable sessions, OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect sign-in, inbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning, and a structured auth event log
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/auth/local.rs — Argon2id-hashed passwords, durable lockout, SHA-256 hashed recovery codes, WebAuthn credentials
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/routes/mfa.rs — the TOTP secret lives only in the encrypted secret store
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/auth/session_revocation.rs — session revocation, including on account deactivation
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/auth/oauth.rs — the OAuth 2.0 / OIDC client for configured identity providers, with client secrets in the encrypted store
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/routes/scim.rs — the inbound SCIM 2.0 provisioning endpoint
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/auth/events.rs — the structured auth event log: sign-in success and failure, lockout, MFA and passkey changes, admin account actions; fail-open but never silent
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/project_authz.rs — per-project reader, writer and administrator roles resolved on every request
claims.notes: Do not name supported identity providers on the public pages; the sign-on module is provider-configurable and the public statement is generic by design.

claims.summary: Every recorded artifact is a signed envelope; significant events go to an append-only, hash-chained ledger whose database privileges allow reading and appending only; the export archive carries the public keys to verify it independently and excludes secrets
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-schemas/src/signed.rs — the Signed<T> envelope: payload hash, key fingerprint, per-producer sequence, Ed25519 signature; not constructible or deserializable outside the crate
fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-controller/migrations/0013_atlas_envelope.sql — SELECT and INSERT only on the envelope chain: append-only is a privilege
fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-controller/migrations/0015_atlas_event_chain.sql — SELECT and INSERT only on the event chain
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/pg_ledger.rs — the evidence ledger read out of PostgreSQL

fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/export/mod.rs — the export archive: ledger, relational data, and trust/ carrying the public keys needed to verify the signatures; credentials and secrets excluded
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 8: the ledger is append-only and cannot be selectively edited; what is deliberately written into it
claims.notes: State the ledger limit wherever deletion is promised. A page that promises full erasure without naming the ledger is wrong.

claims.summary: Download and update integrity: notarized macOS images, Authenticode-signed Windows artifacts, SHA-256 checksums on every asset, and an Ed25519-signed update manifest verified against a key compiled into the download; no SBOM is published
evidence: public-atlas-binaries: README.md — the platform table, the notarization and Authenticode verification commands, SHA256SUMS, latest.json with its detached signature and the pinned public key, and the statement that no SBOM is currently published

fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/update.rs — the manifest is verified against the pinned key before it is parsed; the asset digest is verified before staging and again before apply; server and fleet builds refuse both; every failure resolves to no update
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/config.rs — PACKAGED_UPDATE_PUBKEY_PEM, the update-signing public key compiled into packaged builds
fseven-atlas-mvp: atlas-update.pub.pem — the published public half of the update-signing key
claims.notes: public-atlas-binaries is a public repository that is not checked out in this repository's own CI; its evidence paths are verified wherever it is available and reported as unverified elsewhere.

claims.summary: Atlas contains no analytics, no tracking, and no automatic crash or error reporting; an error report is built in the browser and sent only when the user chooses to send it
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 2, 'What we do not collect'
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/error-log.ts — why nothing transmits on its own
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/diagnostics.ts — the report is assembled field by field from an allowlist and the user chooses to send it
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/package.json — no analytics or telemetry dependency in the application

claims.summary: Usage metering (per-request model, tokens, cost, outcome) is kept for 90 days and is not linked to an individual user
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-llm/src/usage.rs — RETENTION_DAYS = 90 and the purge that enforces it
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 2, usage metering identifies the feature, not the person

claims.summary: The AI provider and model are a configuration choice per feature; on bring-your-own-key plans requests go to the customer's own provider account; F7's promise not to read a key on a hosted instance is a commitment, not an architectural impossibility
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-llm/src/config.rs — provider profiles, per-feature routing, model overrides

fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/secrets.rs — provider keys resolved from the encrypted secret store on every request; AES-256-GCM file store or macOS keychain; the master key kept apart from the encrypted files
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/gateway_client/mod.rs — a bring-your-own-key deployment mints no gateway keypair and opens no session
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 6: the key-access commitment, stated as a commitment rather than an impossibility, with the scoping advice
claims.notes: Never restate the key-access commitment as an architectural guarantee. The in-app policy is deliberate about the difference.

claims.summary: Key custody boundary: F7 ships no hardware security module integration and operates no key-management service; keys live in the instance's encrypted store or an operator-provided module; browser signing uses a non-extractable key; hardware custody, ledger high availability and revocation service levels are not built
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: crates/atlas-cli/src/signer/mod.rs — 'F7 ships no HSM integration and operates no key-management service'; PKCS#11, ssh-agent and Google Cloud KMS clients speak to whatever module the operator points at, whose properties F7 neither provisions nor attests
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/lib/browserSign.ts — the browser signer's key is a non-extractable WebCrypto key the page can use and never read
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/secrets.rs — the instance's encrypted secret store

NOTE: hardware custody, high availability and disaster recovery for the ledger, and revocation service-level commitments are NOT built, and the product's own decision records forbid representing them as shipped
claims.notes: A limitation claim. It is registered so that the public pages keep stating it and so that a future page cannot quietly promote custody to a shipped control.

claims.summary: Voice is off unless configured, requires explicit consent at the point of enabling, and uploads a recording to a third-party speech provider for transcription
evidence: fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/components/VoiceConsentAsk.tsx — the consent step that turning voice on opens first
fseven-atlas-mvp: apis/atlas-serve/src/config.rs — the speech provider configuration (ElevenLabs), inactive until configured
fseven-atlas-mvp: apps/atlas-app/src/legal/privacy-policy.md — section 4, 'Voice, if configured'
claims.notes: The pages say a recording is uploaded for transcription and say nothing about how long the speech provider keeps it; that is governed by the provider's terms.

claims.summary: SOC 2 report, ISO 27001 certification, or independent penetration test report for Atlas
claims.notes: FORBIDDEN CLAIM: no SOC 2 report, no ISO 27001 certificate and no independent penetration test report exist for Atlas. The public pages state each as absent, not planned. Declarative certification claims are rejected by scripts/check-public-claims.sh.
